title: Summary Page Template
eyebrow: Proposal · the summary page shape as a template, and the define-before-use rule

short.lead: You confirmed the grilling summary page (docs/plans/2026-10-19-grilling-summary.html), and the build plan comes next for the restructure in #306 (house-rules: restructure into a shared core with project boundaries and six optional sub-plugins). First, you asked for three things. Keep that page's topic rows as a template for every future grilling session, restructure and brainstorm. Fix the "Requires" box, which held past answers as bare references such as "Round 1 answers 1 and 2". And make one rule apply everywhere: name what a phrase means before using it, or say plainly why you can't. These 4 questions decide how. Once you answer, I will write a plan for the template and the rule change for you to approve, then the restructure's build plan from the new template.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what exists today and what this would change.
items: The page template already has the two boxes

Every page built by the page-building script, make_page.py, uses the plugin's template, templates/handover-page.html. Each topic row opens two boxes: "Creates or changes" and "Requires" (handover-page.html:356-357). The "Requires" box is worded for what a step still needs from you, so on a summary of past answers it reads wrong. The template also has a three-part strip, "What exists today → What this creates → How it impacts you" (handover-page.html:367), used today only in the "What this creates or changes" section.
Questions 1, 2 and 4 below reuse these two boxes and the strip instead of building new ones.
The writing rule already covers part of this

The "Write it so nothing is left to guess" rule (rules/clear-writing.md) already has two bullets on this. "Explicit context" at line 9 says to name the what, where and which. "Named references" at line 12 says never to write "#2" or "option B" alone. Its checker, scripts/clarity.py, flags a bare issue number or option letter (clarity.py:135). It does not flag "round 1, answer 7" or "question 2" with nothing naming what was asked, and no bullet says to define a term before its first use.
Question 3 below decides where your rule goes.
Template, answer wording, rule and how crowded pages are

choices: q1
1. Where is the summary page shape kept as a template?
A

In the plugin, as a starter file for a page's content, templates/decision-summary.page.json. Every grilling, restructure or brainstorm summary starts from it, and on that kind of page the second box is labelled "Decided by" instead of "Requires". Plan pages keep "Requires".
It follows you into every project, because the plugin is installed everywhere, and "Requires" keeps its meaning on plan pages.
B
In this repo only, as an example page under docs/plans/ that I copy by hand each time
Nothing in the plugin changes, but other projects don't get the template, and copying by hand drifts.
In both, the existing page template, templates/handover-page.html, stays the one that draws every page.
q2
2. How does the "Decided by" box name each answer?
A

The round, the question in short form and the answer chosen, in words. For example: "Round 2, question 1, where the agent's name comes from: the GitHub login plus sAgent, which is ajw2003sAgent for you."
Readable on its own, with nothing to look up, and still short enough for a phone.
B
The question and the answer word for word as they appeared on the round's page
Nothing is paraphrased, but long questions make the box several times longer.
In both, a bare reference such as "round 1, answer 7" never appears on its own.
q3
3. Where does your define-before-use rule go?
A

Into the existing "Write it so nothing is left to guess" rule. The "Explicit context" and "Named references" bullets merge into one bullet: name what a phrase means before its first use, so nothing is inferred, and when that genuinely can't be done, say plainly why. The checker, scripts/clarity.py, also flags "answer N", "question N" and "round N" when nothing names what was asked.
Said once, in the rule that already covers replies, pages and issues, and enforced by a checker that already runs on all three.
B
As a new rule of its own in rules/house-rules.md, next to the existing writing rule
It is easier to spot, but two rules then cover the same ground and can drift apart.
In both, the rule applies to everything a person or an AI reads: replies, pages, issues, plans and helper prompts.
q4
4. How does a summary page get less dense?
A
Each topic's "Creates or changes" text becomes short lines of one decision each, and each topic gets the template's existing strip: "What exists today → What this creates → How it impacts you"
It reuses a part the template already draws, and it gives every topic a picture of before and after with no new drawing code.
B
As A, plus a small diagram per topic drawn for that topic
More visual, but every diagram has to be drawn by hand and checked in light and dark mode, on every page.
In both, your define-before-use rule from question 3 still applies to every line.

wrapup.summary: A proposal for keeping the grilling summary page's shape as a template, wording each answer in full, adding your define-before-use rule and making summary pages less dense.
